applicant_utility.summary: This fellowship is not something an individual applies for: an Australian host organisation with a current ABN, working with an overseas counterpart organisation, submits the application and receives the grant of up to AUD 34,500 per fellow plus a co-contribution it must find itself. If you are a mid-career professional, the practical move is to identify and approach an Australian partner organisation that would bid you in as the fellow. Because timing is round-based and Round 22 was expected around Q4 2026 without confirmation in this session, treat the DFAT site - not any listing - as the source for when the window opens.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Australian host organisations with an existing counterpart in a developing country, and mid-career professionals who can sell themselves into that partnership.
application_readiness_checklist: Australian host: confirm the ABN and legal entity status before drafting anything
Document the existing partnership with the overseas counterpart organisation
Build the activity plan around the 2-week minimum in Australia inside a 2-52 week window
Prepare the budget on DFAT's template and evidence the co-contribution explicitly
common_rejection_risks: Fellow is an Australian citizen or permanent resident
Counterpart organisation operating outside an eligible ODA country
No co-contribution from the Australian organisation
Activity with fewer than 2 weeks in Australia, or exceeding 52 weeks
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Everything beyond the grant: the host organisation must fund its co-contribution, and fellows cover personal expenses the activity budget does not include
document_audit: The application is institutional - an individual fellow cannot rescue a weak bid by sending extra documents
Co-contribution evidence must be stated explicitly, not implied in the budget narrative
alerts: Individuals cannot apply directly; all submissions go through the Australian organisation on SmartyGrants
Round dates are the real gate - Round 21 closed 16 January 2026 and Round 22 timing could not be confirmed live
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Australian host organisation applies via SmartyGrants with the counterpart, activity plan, budget and co-contribution evidence.

official.deadline_note: No scholarship application exists; the close dates are unconditional-offer round deadlines. Semester 1, 2027 rounds closed 17 August and 5 October 2026 and close 16 November 2026 (with an additional offer round for IB graduates after 16 December 2026 and International UAC students after 23 December 2026); Semester 2, 2027 rounds close 15 February, 22 March and 3 May 2027.
official.status_note: Automatic consideration applies to eligible students who secure an unconditional offer of admission by the relevant round close date; the scholarship is offered subject to the availability of funds.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The award is a cash scholarship paid in instalments on or after the relevant census date, not a tuition waiver.
official.funding_period: per year (top tier; smaller tiers single-semester)
benefits: Up to $60,000: five tiers of $60,000 or $40,000 payable for one year in two equal instalments per semester, or $20,000, $10,000 or $5,000 payable for one semester
Awarded once during the first year of commencement and not renewable for following years
Availability of some amounts may be limited to specified cohorts
eligibility: International student as defined in the Higher Education Support Act 2003
Applied for but not yet commenced a CRICOS-registered bachelor's degree or coursework master's at the University of Sydney, usually delivered onshore
Received an unconditional offer of admission by the relevant round close date
Recipients of scholarships provided by the Australian Government are not eligible
Students commencing a second degree are eligible provided they have not previously held the Vice Chancellor's International Scholarships
requirements: Complete acceptance of the unconditional offer by the deadline associated with the offer round and remain enrolled after census date
For awards paid in two instalments: maintain a minimum semester average mark (SAM) of 65 and hold no outstanding fees
Recipients on exchange during the award must have achieved a Satisfied Requirements (SR) grade to receive the next payment
documents: No scholarship application or documents - consideration is automatic from the admission application
selection_criteria: Academic merit as assessed from the student's application for admission
Nomination by a selection committee of two nominees of the Executive Director, Sydney Future Students and one nominee of the Admissions Office
Five award amounts assigned based on ranking against the selection criteria
coverage: Five award tiers from $5,000 up to $60,000 based on ranking against the selection criteria
Payment made on or after the relevant census date
application_method: Apply for admission to an eligible University of Sydney coursework degree
Secure an unconditional offer of admission by the relevant round close date - no separate scholarship application is required

official.study_mode: Coursework full degree (bachelor's or postgraduate coursework)

official.description: The Vice-Chancellor's International Scholarships are awarded to exceptional international students commencing an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree at the University of Sydney, and are valued up to $60,000.
official.program_type: Merit scholarship for international coursework students

applicant_utility.summary: There is nothing to apply for here: the money follows your admission offer, so the real task is converting your offer to unconditional before a round closes and presenting the strongest possible academic profile, because the committee ranks you against everyone else in that round. With Semester 1 2027 Round 3 closing 16 November 2026 and Semester 2 rounds running through May 2027, a later start still leaves you in play - but the award pays only in your first year of commencement. Watch the stacking rules: holding a Sydney International Student Award caps VCIS at $40,000, and accepting another University-administered scholarship worth more than A$20,000 per annum terminates this one.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving international students about to commence a University of Sydney bachelor's or coursework master's who already hold, or can quickly secure, an unconditional offer.
application_readiness_checklist: Get your offer unconditional before the round close date - that is the only deadline that matters
Check which tier band your ranking profile falls into; the five amounts are assigned by ranking, not a fixed score
If you also hold a Sydney International Student Award, expect a $40,000 maximum
Accept the offer by the round deadline and stay enrolled past census - payment follows the census date
common_rejection_risks: Holding an Australian Government scholarship - not eligible
Accepting another University-administered scholarship above A$20,000 per annum - terminates VCIS
Dropping below a SAM of 65 before the second instalment
Becoming a domestic student, or commencing part-time study without prior approval
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Most living costs, travel and any fees beyond the instalment value - the award is a cash payment, not a fee waiver or housing guarantee
document_audit: No scholarship documents exist, so the risk is admission-side: a conditional offer or unmet admission conditions block consideration entirely
alerts: The award is once-only during the first year of commencement and is not renewable
Availability of some amounts may be limited to specified cohorts and to available funds
If you exchange during the award you need a Satisfied Requirements grade before your next payment
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Admission application, unconditional offer by the round close date, committee assessment, then instalments on or after each semester's census date - no separate submission.
